usage: A common everyday noun for a neighborhood market; use it when talking about shopping for fresh food and household basics.
It often refers to a wet market in Hong Kong, so it feels more local than a supermarket.
Common collocations include 去街市, 落街市, and 街市買餸.
Natural in daily-errand contexts, especially when describing where you go to buy vegetables, meat, seafood, or fruit.
